diagram_caption: MoE gating network activates top-k feedforward sub-networks per token.

content.tldr: Mixture of Experts (MoE) replaces dense feed-forward layers with multiple specialized subnetworks, using a gating router to dynamically evaluate each token against only a top-k subset of parameters.
content.simple_explanation: In a dense transformer, every single parameter processes every single token. In a sparse Mixture of Experts architecture (such as Mixtral 8x7B), the attention layers remain shared, but the standard feed-forward network is divided into multiple independent 'experts'. A gating router computes a probability distribution over the experts and dispatches the token exclusively to the top-k highest scoring experts (typically top-2), summing their weighted outputs.
content.real_world_example: A hospital triage desk evaluates arriving patients: rather than consulting all eight medical specialists on staff for every minor ailment, the triage nurse routes cardiac symptoms to the cardiologist and fractures to orthopedics.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: MoE allows a model with 45B total parameters to execute with the compute latency and inference cost of a 12B parameter model. However, serving MoE still requires sufficient GPU VRAM to keep all 45B parameters resident, and improper routing can cause severe expert load imbalance.
